kernel.timeouts_and_resumes: kernel.py bounds every make at 1190 s. At host load 15-24 (this run's go test -race and guest suites plus other sessions) both vmlinux stages reached it: first 1196 s, repro 1208 s. The driver then resumed vmlinux on the same O tree. Its settle step looks only for make processes with O= in their arguments, so it did not see the orphaned sub-make children of the killed stage, and resume r1 raced them and failed (first after 68 s: objtool could not open a deleted cpufreq.o; repro after 150 s: fixdep and ar missed files, objtool found evgpeblk.o already processed). Resume r2 started after the orphans had finished and passed (first 181 s; repro 36317 s of wall clock, because the laptop was suspended for about ten hours during it; kernel.py's timeout uses the monotonic clock, which does not count suspend). image-modules and collect then passed as r2 stages. Both packages came out byte-identical (compare_kernel), and the first package differs from the r25 vmlinux in 21 bytes only (20 in .notes, the build ID, and 1 in __bug_table), so the races left no trace in the output. Every stage ran under a user systemd scope with the r17 40-minute bound
